title: 8-round AES-192: herd partial sums, ordered aes-192 for selected subkey recovery

target.description: AES-192 reduced to 8 rounds on 128-bit blocks; initial AddRoundKey k^(0), then rounds 1 through 8, with no MixColumns in the final round. The chosen-byte test uses four initial-key bytes, all 16 bytes of k^(8), and two additional bytes of k'^(7); the remaining needed bytes follow from the AES-192 schedule.

setting.key_relation: One unknown master key with the standard AES expansion; no related-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: Selected near-codebook of 2^128-2^119 distinct plaintexts, forming about 2^23 undamaged herds of 2^104 texts.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.

The paper presents these constructions as attacks on Rijndael. This record prices the explicitly analyzed selected-subkey filter; complete master-key reconstruction and any repeated filter applications are left for a separate completion-budget review.
Guess three final-round columns first, derive two useful equivalent round-seven bytes, and apply the counter reduction before guessing the fourth column. The alternative ordering is slower.

time.note: The source's carefully interleaved AES-192 key guessing gives a 2^16 reduction from the AES-256 2^204 estimate. The separate 2^196 figure belongs to an inferior ordering.

data.note: The near-codebook is acquired once. Testing multiple herds does not mean re-acquiring this codebook once per herd.

memory.reported: Uses the eight-round herd/counter construction; specialized AES-192 peak not separately re-stated
memory.note: The general construction quotes 2^104 bits, then the AES-192 variant changes the order of intermediate counter reductions. The specialized peak is not separately quantified, so no new numeric peak is inferred.

preprocessing.note: Table preparation and setup are described within the construction but not separately priced for this endpoint.

success.description: The exact partial_key_recovery endpoint has no numerical joint success. The zero sum over the entire unpartitioned codebook also holds for wrong guesses and is not a distinguisher; the attack uses correctly partitioned complete herds. The near-codebook construction leaves about half of the herds undamaged, a coverage count rather than a random-selection success rate. The source discusses about26 herd checks for a unique candidate and different AES192/256 schedule costs, without a quantified wrong-key distribution or full-output probability.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit; preserve resource parameters, existing conflicts and full-audit gates. Local source models and conditional relations do not certify whole-output success.

components.description: PDF6–9 Sections2.5–2.6: within a complete herd formed using the correct initial key hypothesis, the targeted byte of b5 sums to zero. For near-codebook data this is conditional on selecting an undamaged herd; it is not a claim about randomly choosing one.

evidence.interpretation: The budget is tied to the stated selected-subkey computation and native operation units. Broad headline claims are retained in the audit report without silently converting a selected-subkey budget into complete master-key recovery.
